process_area.title: Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution

value_stream.name: Customer Construction Debris, Demolition Waste & Site Cleanup Operations

fields.Frequency: Per cleanup job; daily across crews
fields.Trigger: Crew/ container on site per W5444 dispatch

workflows.name: On-Site Debris Collection, Segregation & Load-Out Execution

Automation Opportunity: - Stream-composition photo-estimation; mobile segregation-checklist; contamination-flag prompts at load.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: stream/load accuracy with no hazardous in mixed C&D; load photos required for every job.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE/PPE), W5443 (JHA), W5445 (permit), W5453 (routing/acceptance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Contamination-rejection risk**: a mixed C&D load with food/hazardous is rejected or surcharged at the disposer, eroding margin and delaying the job; mitigated by at-load segregation and crew training.
- **Segregation-labor-cost risk**: over-segregating beyond what the disposer pays for wastes labor; mitigated by stream-segregation rules tied to the destination's acceptance/rebate terms (W5453).
System Touchpoints: - Mobile work-order/stream-capture app; container/load photo store; dispatch (W5444); VS-24 JHA.
Time Estimate: - ~1–4 hours/job on-site depending on volume/access; crew of 2–4.

steps.activity: On arrival, verify site access, JHA/PPE (W5443), container placement permit (W5445), and the work-order scope/exclusions.
Segregate debris at load-out into streams: clean wood, drywall, concrete/masonry/tile rubble, metals, packaging/plastic, cardboard, and a separate hazardous-discovery pile.
Load container/truck by stream (single-stream mixed if disposal route accepts; multi-stream if diversion targets require separation).
Minimize contamination (no food/general waste, no hazardous in mixed C&D) — contaminated loads are rejected by recyclers/landfills and incur surcharges.
Capture load photos, stream composition estimate, and time-on-site for the work order (W5457).

fields.Participants: Crew, HSE (VS-24), customer, neighbors/HOA, LGU (VS-76), PCAB (VS-165)
fields.Trigger: Demolition-phase job (interior demo, full structure, post-disaster VS-184)
fields.Volume: Larger/heavier debris loads; longer on-site duration

workflows.name: Demolition Debris Load-Out, Dust/Noise & Neighbor Management

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-scope lock-in the work order; hour-restricted-work alerts; complaint-tracking integration.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: noisy work only within LGU-permitted hours.
Cross-references: - links to VS-165 (PCAB/RA 4566), VS-76 (LGU), VS-24 (HSE), VS-186 (heavy equipment), VS-74 (heavy delivery), VS-184 (post-disaster)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-demolition risk**: crew removes a load-bearing or out-of-scope element causing structural/utility damage; mitigated by scope-locked execution and customer-PM sign-off.
- **Neighbor-complaint/LGU-fine risk**: dust/noise outside permitted hours triggers complaints, LGU fines, or work stoppage; mitigated by hour-limited execution and active neighbor management.
System Touchpoints: - LGU/PCAB permit records (VS-165/VS-76/VS-166); JHA (VS-24); heavy-haul dispatch (VS-186/VS-74); work-order (W5448).
Time Estimate: - ~0.5–3 days/demo job depending on scale; heavy-haul coordination adds lead time.

steps.activity: Confirm demolition scope vs. PCAB/permit coverage (VS-165) and the LGU demolition/building permit; do not exceed the permitted scope.
Deploy dust/noise/vibration controls (water suppression, tarps, scheduling noisy work within allowed hours, debris chute).
Notify neighbors/HOA per LGU/condominium requirements and manage complaints through the escalation path.
Sequence demolition to preserve structural elements per plan (load-bearing, shared walls) and protect utilities.
Load demolition debris (heavier rubble, mixed) — possibly requiring heavy haul (VS-186 equipment, VS-74 heavy delivery) — and route per W5453.

fields.Trigger: Load departs site; arrival at disposer/transfer; billing

workflows.name: C&D Debris Weight/Volume Verification & Weighbridge Ticket Capture

Automation Opportunity: - Weight-ticket OCR/digital ingest; auto-reconciliation vs estimate; diversion-stream auto-classification.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: weight/volume accuracy with manifest/weight-ticket evidence; certified-scale requirement (VS-115).
Cross-references: - links to VS-115 W3626 (scale calibration), VS-15 (billing), VS-11 (project billing), W5447 (disposer), W5459 (diversion analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dispute-on-weight risk**: customer disputes the hauling fee because the load weight differs from the estimate; mitigated by weighbridge ticket evidence and conservative estimation (W5442).
- **Mismeasurement risk**: an uncalibrated or non-certified weighbridge produces inaccurate weights that distort billing and diversion reporting; mitigated by certified-scale verification (VS-115).
System Touchpoints: - Weighbridge/weight-ticket ingest (VS-115 W3626 calibrated); manifest system (W5452); work-order/billing (VS-15/VS-11); diversion analytics (W5459).

steps.activity: Capture the load's volume estimate at load-out (W5449) and verify against container/truck capacity.
At the weighbridge/disposer, capture the certified weight ticket (VS-115 W3626 scale calibration ensures accuracy); reconcile to volume estimate.
Record weight/volume, stream composition, and disposal/processing destination against the manifest (W5452).
Flag discrepancies (significant overweight/underweight vs. estimate, unexpected stream) for investigation.
Feed verified weights into billing/settlement (W5457) and the diversion analytics (W5459).

workflows.name: DENR-Compliant C&D Transporter Permitting & Hauling Manifest

Automation Opportunity: - Digital manifest generation; chain-of-custody e-signature; auto-retention and ESG/ regulatory aggregation.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: no C&D load dispatched without a manifest.
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (DENR compliance), VS-166 (permit portfolio), VS-88 (records), VS-25 (ESG reporting), VS-187 (hazardous TSD), W5447 (vendor accreditation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Missing-manifest risk**: a load hauled without a manifest breaks the chain-of-custody and exposes BuildRight to illegal-dumping liability if the hauler mis-disposes; mitigated by no-manifest-no-dispatch gating.
- **Mis-classified-stream risk**: labeling a regulated/hazardous stream as "C&D" to avoid TSD routing breaches RA 6969; mitigated by the W5443 pre-job screen and W5454 discovery rerouting.
System Touchpoints: - Manifest system (DENR-aligned); transporter/disposer accreditation (VS-166/VS-22); records retention (VS-88); ESG reporting (VS-25); billing (VS-15).
Time Estimate: - ~5–10 min/load manifest generation; periodic aggregation ~1 day/month.

steps.activity: Confirm the transporter is DENR-registered / LGU-permitted for C&D hauling (W5447 onboarding; VS-166 permit portfolio).
Generate a hauling manifest per load: origin, stream composition, volume/weight, transporter, destination (recycler/MDRF/landfill), and generator (BuildRight on behalf of customer).
Capture chain-of-custody signatures/stamps (origin → transporter → disposer) — digital where the disposer supports it.
Retain manifests per DENR (RA 6969/RA 9003) and BIR (W590 fuel/expense) record-retention (VS-88; 10-yr per BIR).
Aggregate manifests for DENR/LGU periodic reporting and ESG disclosure (VS-25).

workflows.name: Multi-Stream Routing to Recycler / Reprocessor / MDRF / Landfill

Automation Opportunity: - Stream-to-destination auto-routing rules; rebate/recovery auto-capture; diversion-impact modeling.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: divertible streams routed to recovery, not landfill, where accredited capacity exists.
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG), VS-179 (EPR/circular), VS-73 (circular economy), W5447 (accredited disposer), W5459 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Landfill-avoidable risk**: routing divertible streams to landfill forfeits recovery value and ESG credit; mitigated by stream-to-destination rules and diversion targets.
- **Destination-capacity risk**: a recycler/MDRF closes or hits capacity, stranding a stream; mitigated by fallback destinations (W5447) and capacity monitoring.
System Touchpoints: - Routing/destination rules engine; disposer accreditation (W5447); ESG reporting (VS-25); settlement (W5457); analytics (W5459).
Time Estimate: - ~10 min/load routing decision; periodic optimization ~1 week/quarter.

steps.activity: Route each segregated stream to its highest-value/accredited destination: clean wood → biomass/repurposer; metals → scrap recycler (recovery value); concrete/masonry → crusher/reprocessor; drywall/cardboard → recycler; residuals → accredited sanitary landfill/MDRF.
Match destination to the customer's/project's diversion target (W5446) and BuildRight's ESG goal (VS-25).
Capture destination acceptance/rejection and any rebates (scrap-metal recovery, reprocessor credits) for settlement (W5457).
Optimize routing over time for cost/diversion/distance (route clean wood to the nearest biomass plant, etc.).
Report diversion by stream and destination into ESG (VS-25) and the analytics (W5459).

fields.Frequency: Ad-hoc / event-driven — non-trivial frequency in older-stock/post-disaster jobs
fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), VS-187 hazmat TSD, VS-73 abatement (W2613), Compliance (VS-22), customer
fields.Trigger: Crew discovers suspect/regulated material during the job (not caught in W5443 screen)
fields.Volume: ~10–20% of demolition/older-stock jobs discover some regulated material

workflows.name: Hazardous / Regulated Debris Discovery & Rerouting During Cleanup

Automation Opportunity: - Suspect-material identification app (photo → likely classification → routing); auto-change-order generation; recurring-discovery feed to the pre-job screen.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: crew trained to stop-isolate-escalate on any suspect material.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-73 W2613 (asbestos/lead), VS-187 (hazmat TSD), VS-143 (refrigerant), VS-114 (DG transport), W5443 (pre-job screen)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Co-mingling-contamination risk**: regulated material swept into a standard C&D load contaminates the whole load (rejected, surcharged, or a DENR violation); mitigated by stop-isolate-route discipline.
- **Customer-dispute-on-scope risk**: discovered hazardous material expands scope/cost mid-job; mitigated by clear change-order terms (W5448) and transparent customer communication.
System Touchpoints: - JHA/hazard module (VS-24); regulated-waste manifest (VS-187/VS-114); abatement records (VS-73 W2613); work-order change (W5448); compliance records (VS-22).
Time Estimate: - ~immediate stop + ~2–8 hours/ discovery to identify, isolate, and reroute.

steps.activity: Crew stops work on the suspect material and isolates it; contacts the supervisor/HSE for identification (asbestos/lead suspect, paint/solvent, chemical container, refrigerant, treated/e-waste).

HSE/Compliance identify the material and route to the correct handling path: asbestos/lead abatement (VS-73 W2613); household hazardous TSD (VS-187); refrigerant recovery (VS-143); e-waste (VS-187/VS-99).
Exclude the material from the mixed C&D load and manifest it under the appropriate regulated-waste manifest (DENR RA 6969 / VS-114 DG transport if applicable).
Inform the customer, adjust the work order/scope/price (W5448 change order), and document the discovery and resolution.
Feed recurring discoveries into the W5443 pre-job screen to improve future hazard detection.

fields.Participants: Customer, Services Manager, Quality (VS-31), VS-146 mystery-shop (service quality)
fields.Trigger: Debris hauled; site ready for handover

workflows.name: Site Final Cleanup, Handover & Customer Sign-Off

Automation Opportunity: - Before/after photo auto-capture; digital sign-off; punch-list auto-tracking to settlement; automated survey trigger.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: handover/sign-off evidence; no settlement without signed customer sign-off (revenue recognition at completion).
Cross-references: - links to VS-31 (quality), VS-146 (service quality/mystery shop), VS-13 (customer survey), VS-157 (revenue recognition), W5457 (settlement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incomplete-handover risk**: customer later disputes that cleanup was incomplete, withholding payment; mitigated by signed sign-off + before/after photo evidence.
- **Punch-list-creep risk**: open punch-list items never close, delaying settlement; mitigated by defined punch-list owner/timeline and settlement-on-closure.
System Touchpoints: - Mobile work-order/quality-checklist app; photo store; customer sign-off capture; survey (VS-13/VS-146); revenue recognition (VS-157).

steps.activity: Perform the final site sweep/broom-clean, remove residual debris/dust, and restore the work area (surface protection removal, furniture repositioning).
Inspect against the work-order scope and a quality checklist; capture before/after photos for handover and dispute defense.
Walk the site with the customer, confirm scope completion, and obtain signed sign-off (digital via app).
Log any punch-list items with owner and timeline; close the punch-list before final settlement (W5457).
Trigger post-service survey (VS-146/VS-13) and revenue recognition at completion (VS-157/W5448).

fields.Trigger: Hauling operations; spill/accident event; route/permit change

workflows.name: Hauling Safety, Spill Response & Road/Route Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - Telematics-based securement/cover monitoring; truck-ban-aware routing; auto-incident notification.
Controls: - CTL-804 (ensure controlled execution — Debris Collection, Segregation & DENR-Compliant Hauling Execution (PA-191.2).)
- operational: tarped/secured load required for every C&D trip.
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (fleet/driver safety), VS-24 (spill/HSE), VS-114 (DG transport), VS-22 (LGU/DENR), VS-26 (insurance), VS-110 (freight)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Road-litter/falling-debris risk**: an un-tarped C&D load sheds debris on public roads, causing accidents and LGU fines; mitigated by mandatory tarping/securement and telematics monitoring.
- **Truck-ban-violation risk**: hauling during LGU truck-ban hours results in fines/impoundment; mitigated by route/time planning and dispatch enforcement.
System Touchpoints: - Fleet/telematics (VS-06 W199); route planning (VS-06 W1369); spill-response plan (VS-24); DG transport (VS-114); insurance (VS-26); HSE incident system (VS-24).
Time Estimate: - ~5–10 min/trip route/securement check; spill response per severity (minutes–hours).

steps.activity: Enforce load securement (tarped/covered C&D to prevent road litter), vehicle roadworthiness, and driver qualification/hours (VS-06 W197/W1400 driver compliance).
Plan routes to comply with LGU truck bans / weight-restricted roads / time-of-day restrictions (links VS-06 W1369/W1228).
Maintain a spill-response plan for C&D (dust/debris release, minor chemical if co-mingled) integrated with VS-24 spill and VS-114 DG where applicable.
Respond to spills/accidents: contain, document, notify LGU/DENR per severity (VS-22), and coordinate insurance (VS-26).
Report hauling-safety incidents/metrics into HSE (VS-24) and fleet analytics (VS-06/VS-61).
